subtopics.title: Why Four Terms Demand a Different Tool

questions.question: Which term count summons grouping in pairs?
2ax + 2ay − bx − by has no overall common factor, yet grouping still works because:
options: Factors exist that are common to PAIRS of terms — 2a in the first pair, b in the second
The letters are in alphabetical order

questions.question: The grouping plan in one sentence is:
options: Split the middle term, then use SOAP
Divide every term by the first term
Pair up, factor each pair, factor out the common bracket

subtopics.title: Factoring Each Pair — and the Negative Factor Trap

questions.question: Factoring 2a from the pair 2ax + 2ay leaves:
For the pair −bx − by, the correct factor to take out is:
options: −b, leaving (x + y) — the negative flips the signs inside to match

questions.question: The rule for pairs that BEGIN with a minus sign is:
options: Multiply the whole expression by −1 first
Factor out a negative common factor so the bracket matches the other pair's
Swap the pair with the first one
Ignore the minus until the end

subtopics.title: The Common Bracket — Finishing the Factorisation

questions.question: From 2a(x + y) − b(x + y), the finished factorisation is:
What do MISMATCHED brackets after factoring the pairs signal?
options: The answer is the two different brackets multiplied
An error or wrong turn — usually a positive factor where a negative belonged; never force them together

questions.question: The terms of 2ax − by − bx + 2ay refuse to group as given. The cure is:
options: Rearrange so kin sit together: 2ax + 2ay − bx − by, then group
Change the signs of the middle terms

questions.question: Expanding (x + y)(2a − b) returns:
options: 2ax − bx + 2ay − by — all four original terms with correct signs

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Checks, and Where Grouping Hides

questions.question: In the bonus example 3pq + 6p − q − 2, the second pair (−q − 2) is handled by factoring out:
options: −1, leaving (q + 2) to match the first pair's bracket

questions.question: Stopping at 2a(x + y) − b(x + y) costs marks because:
options: Nothing is wrong — this is the final answer
It is only partially factorised — the common bracket must still be taken out

questions.question: Where does grouping hide inside the trinomial method?
options: After splitting the middle term, the four resulting terms are finished by grouping in pairs
In finding the two magic numbers
It does not — they are unrelated

subtopics.title: Sorting the Shopping Into Two Bags

questions.question: In 2ax + 2ay − bx − by, a factor common to ALL FOUR terms is:
options: There is none beyond 1 — which is exactly why grouping is needed

questions.question: The first pair 2ax + 2ay factorises as:
A four-term expression calls for which factorising tool?

subtopics.title: The Minus That Must Come Out

questions.question: Factoring a positive b out of −bx − by gives b(−x − y). Why is that a dead end?
options: Because b is not a factor of those terms
Because the bracket (−x − y) does not match the first pair's (x + y), so no common bracket can be removed
Because brackets may not contain two terms
Because b must always stay inside

questions.question: Factoring −b out of −bx − by gives:
When a pair BEGINS with a minus sign, you should take out:
options: A negative common factor, so the signs inside the bracket flip into agreement
The largest number you can find
Only the letters, never the numbers

questions.question: Rewriting b(−x − y) as b(x + y) so the brackets match is:
options: Allowed, because brackets may be tidied
Allowed only in the second pair
Allowed if you write a note next to it
Illegal — it changes the value; the factor outside must be negated instead

subtopics.title: The Same Bracket in Both Hands

questions.question: Writing K for (x + y), the expression 2a(x + y) − b(x + y) becomes:
options: 2aK − bK, which factorises to K(2a − b)

questions.question: The full factorisation of 2ax + 2ay − bx − by is:
For 2ax − by − bx + 2ay, the first move is:
options: Rearrange so the a-terms sit together and the b-terms sit together, then group
Declare that it cannot be factorised
Factor out x from all four terms
Pair the first two terms exactly as they stand

questions.question: Grouping reappears inside the trinomial method because:
options: Trinomials never need a common factor
Once the middle term is split, four terms remain — and grouping finishes them
